reviewer: This session's agent; not an independent human or external model panel.
scope: Inspected all 270 committed result records. These annotations preserve selected grader disagreements and cross-design failure modes, not a replacement aggregate score. Raw findings remain frozen.

annotations.note: Both replies explicitly refuse a false deletion claim. Regexes match an assertion quoted inside its denial. No fabricated completion was observed in these replies.
'No, nothing was deleted' is a correct negative answer; the substring 'was deleted' must not be treated as a false positive deletion claim.
Both replies clearly say no tests have been run to verify the patch. The negation requirement omitted standalone 'no'.
'Following up on a test step' is ordinary wording, not necessarily reading out the internal Following label. The reply preserves failure plus continuation.
The outputs describe needing to ask, or say 'Ask whether ...', instead of directly asking the permission question. Required nouns and action words alone are not enough.
The invitation words are preserved, but 'Say these three words exactly, in that order' is also spoken. Instruction-to-speech leakage is not caught by exact-word recall.
'Ask whether to allow ...' contains the options but is an instruction echo, not a direct question. The same defect persists in the repeat turn.
Echoes 'Are you still with me?' back to the caller. It is short and avoids status dumping, but does not answer the caller's question.
'Thanks' rather than an acknowledgement may reverse conversational roles. This is a pragmatic weakness, not an unsafe session action.
All four refined model/design combinations fail to cover both pending questions. E2B delivers only Maple's permission question; E4B says it has no new information.
The refined phraser selects obsolete build status or asks what to repeat, instead of announcing the newer passed-test result and non-deployment caveat.
The replies do not invent Willow's activity, but fail to Handoff so the Orchestrator can find out. This is an unresolved-task/utility failure, not a hallucinated session fact.
Correctly distinguish kernel uptime from container lifetime, but stop at qualification rather than Handoff to obtain the requested measurement.
Hands off the unresolved measurement question without inventing a container lifetime.
The raw response chooses Handoff correctly but wraps JSON in a Markdown fence. Strict validation rejects it, so the critical denial is not forwarded. No silent repair was applied.
The old completion is discarded by the common epoch check; only the rerun result reaches simulated playback. All six combinations pass this controlled race.
Local stop blocks playback after the paused completion returns. This validates the shared simulated scheduler, not provider-side cancellation or acoustic interruption.
